headline: Senate Agrees to Move Sara Duterte Impeachment Trial to Afternoons
seoTitle: Senate Agrees to Afternoon Sara Duterte Impeachment Hearings | FMB News
seoDescription: Senator-judges agreed to move regular Senate business to the morning and hold longer impeachment trial hearings in the afternoon.
deck: The schedule change is intended to allow longer hearings and support the Senate's target of completing the trial before the end of 2026.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said senator-judges had reached a consensus to move regular legislative sessions to the morning and hold longer impeachment trial hearings in the afternoon.

The plan would allow the impeachment court to open around 3 p.m. after legislative work, rather than limiting trial proceedings to the morning. Gatchalian said the adjustment would be implemented within the week.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The Senate is trying to prevent the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte from extending into 2027. Gatchalian said the chamber is targeting one witness per day and hopes to reach a verdict by December.

Day 17 proceeded on August 24 with former Office of the Vice President special disbursing officer Gina Acosta completing her testimony. The trial concerns allegations involving the use of confidential funds; the charges remain subject to adjudication by the impeachment court.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: A longer daily trial window could speed up witness examination while allowing the Senate to continue its regular legislative work, including deliberations on the proposed 2027 national budget.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for the Senate's formal daily calendar confirming when the revised schedule takes effect, the next prosecution witness and any rulings that alter the pace of the proceedings.
